**Thu 08.10.26, 14:15–15:45 · Room 4.B51** · Basic reading: KW ch. 5 (pp. 104–124) · Applied reading: Little & Meng (2023), *Measuring democratic backsliding* · Presenters: **Nuraida Abdykapar Kyzy, Simon Ferdinand Eibach, Martins Titilola**

**Learning goals:** students can (1) tell a concept from a variable and explain operationalization; (2) define reliability and face, content and construct validity; (3) explain why more data reduces random error but not bias.

**Before class:** presentation slides in OLAT (due Wed 07.10, 12:00)? · seminar questions 3 and 4 uploaded? · grading sheet printed (`00_grading/presentation_grading_sheet.pdf`) · count of missing R tracks (`00_admin/track_choices.csv`) · deck in speaker view (press S)

**Discussion prompts (if the room is quiet):** Is an "objective" indicator unbiased? Incumbents can also lose for performance reasons (p. 158). · Are elections and turnover all of democracy (content validity)? · Can coder bias change over time, and why does that matter more than constant bias (KW p. 114 vs. Little & Meng p. 152)? · Population weights or unweighted country averages (p. 151)? · What would the presenters' alternative design measure, and how reliably?

**Grading (0–5 each, 15/30 = pass):** clarity · understanding · critique quality · reasoning · feasibility · discussion. Three presenters, one grade.
